h1:
Wat Rong Suea Ten
Chiang Rai's Blue Temple
intro: If Wat Rong Khun is the White Temple, Wat Rong Suea Ten is the Blue Temple that most people pair it with on the same trip. This sapphire-blue hall trimmed in gold is the work of Sala Nok, a student in Ajarn Chalermchai's lineage, and it sits along the Kok River a short hop from town. We've pulled together the opening hours, entry, how to get there and the best photo spots all in one place.

blocks.html: Wat Rong Suea Ten is the only temple in Chiang Rai with a hall in deep sapphire blue. It was designed by Sala Nok (Phuttha Kabkaew), a local artist who once worked on the White Temple alongside Ajarn Chalermchai Kositpipat. The hall uses sapphire blue cut with gold and white detailing, and the whole thing reads almost like flowing water. It took around 10 years to build and was finished in early 2016. These days it's one of those stops almost every Chiang Rai trip ends up making for a photo.

items: Opening hours — daily, roughly 7:00am–8:00pm (in the evening the hall is lit up and the blue takes on a different look)
Entry — no admission fee; it's free to enter, with a donation box if you'd like to make merit
Location — Rong Suea Ten community, Rim Kok subdistrict, Mueang district, Chiang Rai — under 10 minutes from the city centre by car

blocks.title: Before you enter the hall
blocks.html: This is still an active temple, so dress modestly — skip spaghetti straps and very short shorts — and take your shoes off before going up into the hall. Keep your voice down and don't climb on the sculptures for photos.

What makes this place stand out is the sapphire blue set against gold, a colour combination you rarely see in a Thai temple. There are several spots people like to shoot — it's worth walking the whole grounds first and picking your light.

items.name: Naga staircase out front
items.blurb: Two nagas with blue-green scales run the length of the staircase. It's the first spot everyone stops at, and it works for both portrait and wide shots.

items.name: Blue walls and archways
items.blurb: Gold stucco detailing over a deep blue base makes a seriously colourful backdrop — good for getting a person in frame with the architecture.

items.name: Upagupta in the pond
items.blurb: A pearl-white Buddha image sits in the middle of a fountain, ringed by blue sculpted fish — a nice contrast against the temple's main palette.

items.name: Inside the hall
items.blurb: Inside is the pearl-white principal Buddha, Phra Phuttha Ratchamongkol Bodi Trilokanat, with a lap width of 5m and a height of 6.5m. Photos are fine inside, but skip the flash and anything that disturbs people who've come to pray.

blocks.text: Getting there and when to go

items: Own car / rental — easiest option. From town take the Chiang Rai–Mae Sai road; it's about 300m past the Khun Korn bridge, with parking out front.
Songthaew / taxi / Grab — easy to grab from town, and since it's close the fare isn't much — handy if you're not driving yourself
Pair it with other temples — it's on the same route as Wat Huay Pla Kang and Wat Rong Khun, so you can easily roll all three into one day of temple-and-art hopping
Best time to go — mornings are quieter for photos, the afternoon sun makes the blue pop, and after dark the hall is lit for a different mood

blocks.title: Beating the crowds
blocks.html: Long weekends and festivals get packed. If you want clean shots without people, aim for early morning right after it opens, or late afternoon on a weekday.

faq.q: What time does Wat Rong Suea Ten open?
faq.a: It's open daily, roughly 7:00am–8:00pm. In the evening the hall is lit up, giving the blue a different feel. It's worth checking the temple's page again before you go if there's a merit-making event on.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for Wat Rong Suea Ten?
faq.a: No, entry is free. There's a donation box if you'd like to make merit and help with the temple's upkeep and restoration.

faq.q: What's the difference between Wat Rong Suea Ten and Wat Rong Khun?
faq.a: Wat Rong Khun is the white temple by Ajarn Chalermchai, while Wat Rong Suea Ten is the blue temple by Sala Nok, who once worked with him. That's why a lot of people visit both on the same trip.

faq.q: What should I wear to the temple?
faq.a: Dress modestly — skip spaghetti straps and very short shorts. Take your shoes off before going up into the hall, and keep noise down, as this is still an active place of worship.

faq.q: How long do I need to visit?
faq.a: Walking around and taking photos usually takes about 45 minutes to an hour. It's a good stop on the way to Wat Huay Pla Kang or Wat Rong Khun on a single-day trip.
